1925-07-01.head: Nationalist Government Proclaimed at Canton
1925-07-01.body: The Kuomintang has proclaimed a National Government of the Republic of China at Canton, in rivalry with the Peking authorities.

1925-07-01.head: Dutch Coalition Loses Ground at Polls
1925-07-01.body: Elections for the Second Chamber of the Netherlands States-General have cut the governing coalition's majority from 59 to 54 of the 100 seats.

1925-07-01.head: Death of Erik Satie
1925-07-01.body: M. Erik Satie, 59, the French composer, has died in Paris.

1925-07-02.head: Last Tsarist Premier Shot by Soviets
1925-07-02.body: Prince Nikolai Golitsyn, the last Prime Minister of Imperial Russia, has been executed by the Soviet authorities.

1925-07-02.head: Radiology Congress Opens in London
1925-07-02.body: The first International Congress of Radiology has been sitting in London, attended by physicians from many nations.
1925-07-02.note: Congress opened 1 July; carried as continuing news.

1925-07-03.head: Mlle Lenglen Wins Sixth Wimbledon Title
1925-07-03.body: Mlle Suzanne Lenglen of France defeated Miss Joan Fry of England in the ladies' singles final at Wimbledon, taking her sixth championship.

1925-07-04.head: Lacoste Takes Wimbledon Crown
1925-07-04.body: M. René Lacoste defeated his countryman M. Jean Borotra in the men's singles final at Wimbledon, completing a French double.

1925-07-04.head: Boston Club Collapse Kills Forty-Four
1925-07-04.body: The Pickwick Club in Boston collapsed during an Independence Day dance, killing 44 people.

1925-07-05.head: Amundsen Welcomed Home in Oslo
1925-07-05.body: Captain Roald Amundsen, Mr Lincoln Ellsworth and their companions received a heroes' welcome in Oslo on returning from their attempted flight to the North Pole.

1925-07-06.head: Treasury of St Peter's Robbed
1925-07-06.body: Police in Rome have reported that the treasury of St Peter's Basilica was robbed of valuables estimated at five to seven million lire.

1925-07-07.head: Berlin Protests Soviet Death Sentences
1925-07-07.body: The German Government has sent a strong note of protest to Moscow over the sentencing to death of three German students.

1925-07-08.head: Hong Kong Strike and Boycott Continues
1925-07-08.body: The general strike and boycott against British trade at Hong Kong and Canton has continued, paralysing the colony's commerce.
1925-07-08.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-07-09.head: Military Coup in Ecuador
1925-07-09.body: Young army officers in Ecuador have overthrown President Gonzalo Córdova and installed a military junta at Quito.

1925-07-10.head: Evolution Trial Opens in Tennessee
1925-07-10.body: The trial of Mr John T. Scopes, a schoolmaster charged with teaching evolution contrary to Tennessee law, has opened at Dayton.

1925-07-10.head: Soviet Telegraph Agency Founded
1925-07-10.body: The Soviet Government has established the Telegraph Agency of the Soviet Union (TASS) as its official news agency.

1925-07-11.head: Dayton Trial Draws World Attention
1925-07-11.body: The Scopes evolution trial at Dayton, Tennessee, has drawn crowds and correspondents from many countries, with Mr W. J. Bryan assisting the prosecution.
1925-07-11.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-07-12.head: French Arrest Druze Chiefs in Syria
1925-07-12.body: French authorities have arrested three sheikhs of the al-Atrash family of the Jabal Druze, summoned under the guise of negotiations. Sultan al-Atrash is reported raising followers.

1925-07-13.head: Darrow Attacks Tennessee Evolution Law
1925-07-13.body: Mr Clarence Darrow, for the defence at Dayton, delivered a lengthy address urging the court to quash the indictment as an attack on freedom of thought.
1925-07-13.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-07-14.head: Boxing Champion Pancho Villa Dies
1925-07-14.body: Pancho Villa, 23, the Filipino flyweight champion of the world, has died in San Francisco of an infection following dental treatment.

1925-07-15.head: Scopes Pleads Not Guilty
1925-07-15.body: At Dayton the court refused to quash the indictment, and Mr Scopes entered a plea of not guilty as the evolution trial proceeded.
1925-07-15.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-07-16.head: King Feisal Opens First Iraqi Parliament
1925-07-16.body: King Feisal has opened the first Parliament of Iraq at Baghdad.

1925-07-16.head: Mosul Commission Reports to League
1925-07-16.body: The League of Nations commission of inquiry on the Mosul frontier has completed its report on the dispute between Turkey and Great Britain over the vilayet.

1925-07-17.head: Hong Kong Landslide Buries Houses
1925-07-17.body: A retaining wall gave way after heavy rain at Po Hing Fong, Hong Kong, bringing down houses and killing about 75 persons.

1925-07-18.head: Hitler Publishes Book in Munich
1925-07-18.body: The first volume of Adolf Hitler's book 'Mein Kampf' has been published in Munich.

1925-07-18.head: Druze Down French Aeroplane
1925-07-18.body: Druze followers of Sultan al-Atrash brought down a French reconnaissance aeroplane near Mitin and captured its two airmen.

1925-07-19.head: Bottecchia Wins Tour de France Again
1925-07-19.body: Ottavio Bottecchia of Italy has won the Tour de France cycle race for the second year in succession.

1925-07-20.head: Druze Rebels Seize Salkhad
1925-07-20.body: Sultan al-Atrash's forces have captured Salkhad, the second town of the Jabal Druze, in revolt against French rule.

1925-07-20.head: Bryan Questioned on Bible at Dayton
1925-07-20.body: Mr W. J. Bryan took the stand at the Scopes trial and was examined by Mr Darrow on the literal truth of the Bible.

1925-07-21.head: Scopes Found Guilty, Fined $100
1925-07-21.body: Mr John T. Scopes was found guilty at Dayton, Tennessee, of teaching the theory of evolution and fined $100.

1925-07-21.head: Campbell Exceeds 150 Miles an Hour
1925-07-21.body: Captain Malcolm Campbell became the first man to drive a motor car at more than 150 miles an hour, on Pendine Sands, Wales.

1925-07-22.head: French Column Destroyed at al-Kafr
1925-07-22.body: Druze horsemen under Sultan al-Atrash ambushed a French column of some 166 men under Captain Normand at al-Kafr; most of the soldiers were killed.

1925-07-22.head: Suwayda Garrison Besieged
1925-07-22.body: The rebels have laid siege to the French garrison in the citadel of Suwayda, chief town of the Jabal Druze.

1925-07-23.head: Druze Revolt Spreads in Jabal
1925-07-23.body: The French garrison at Suwayda remained besieged as volunteers flocked to Sultan al-Atrash, who is reported master of the Jabal Druze.
1925-07-23.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-07-24.head: Palestine Citizenship Order Made
1925-07-24.body: The British Government has made the Palestinian Citizenship Order, 1925, defining nationality in the mandated territory.

1925-07-25.head: Coal Crisis Deepens in Britain
1925-07-25.body: British mine owners' notices ending the 1924 wages agreement are due to expire on 31 July, and the miners have refused the proposed reductions.
1925-07-25.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-07-26.head: W. J. Bryan Dies at Dayton
1925-07-26.body: Mr William Jennings Bryan, 65, thrice Democratic candidate for President and former Secretary of State, died in his sleep at Dayton five days after the Scopes trial.

1925-07-26.head: Death of Gottlob Frege
1925-07-26.body: Professor Gottlob Frege, 76, the German logician and mathematician, has died.

1925-07-27.head: Daventry Long-Wave Station Opened
1925-07-27.body: The British Broadcasting Company has opened its high-power long-wave transmitter at Daventry, the first of its kind in the world.

1925-07-27.head: American Correspondent Expelled from Italy
1925-07-27.body: Mr George Seldes, correspondent of the Chicago Tribune, has been ordered to leave Italy by the Fascist authorities.

1925-07-28.head: Miners and Owners Deadlocked
1925-07-28.body: Negotiations between the British coal owners and the Miners' Federation remained deadlocked, with transport unions pledged to support the miners.
1925-07-28.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-07-29.head: Siege of Suwayda Continues
1925-07-29.body: The French garrison in the citadel of Suwayda remained cut off by Druze rebels, and French reinforcements were reported gathering at Damascus.
1925-07-29.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-07-30.head: Government Weighs Coal Subsidy
1925-07-30.body: The British Cabinet has been in conference with miners and owners as the lock-out notices in the coalfields approach expiry.
1925-07-30.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-07-31.head: Coal Stoppage Averted by Subsidy
1925-07-31.body: The British Government has announced a subsidy to the coal industry for nine months to maintain wages, averting a national stoppage. A Royal Commission will inquire into the industry.

1925-07-31.head: Last French Troops Quit the Ruhr
1925-07-31.body: The last French and Belgian troops have left the Ruhr district.

1925-08-01.head: Palestine Citizenship Order in Force
1925-08-01.body: The Palestinian Citizenship Order, 1925, has come into effect in the British Mandate for Palestine.

1925-08-01.head: British Seamen Strike Over Pay Cut
1925-08-01.body: Many British seamen have struck work after their monthly wage was cut from £10 to £9.

1925-08-01.head: New Portuguese Ministry
1925-08-01.body: Senhor Domingos Leite Pereira has become Prime Minister of Portugal for the third time.

1925-08-02.head: Druze Attack French at al-Mazraa
1925-08-02.body: Druze and Bedouin horsemen have attacked the French relief column under General Michaud at al-Mazraa, on its march to Suwayda.

1925-08-03.head: French Column Routed in Jabal Druze
1925-08-03.body: General Michaud's column has been thrown back at al-Mazraa with heavy losses, abandoning rifles, machine guns and artillery to the Druze.

1925-08-03.head: Fascists Win Sicilian Local Elections
1925-08-03.body: The Fascists have won the local elections in Sicily, with Blackshirts stationed at the polling places.

1925-08-04.head: American Marines Leave Nicaragua
1925-08-04.body: The last United States Marines have been withdrawn from Nicaragua after thirteen years.

1925-08-04.head: Colijn Forms Dutch Cabinet
1925-08-04.body: Dr Hendrikus Colijn has become Prime Minister of the Netherlands.

1925-08-05.head: Mustafa Kemal Divorces Wife
1925-08-05.body: President Mustafa Kemal of Turkey has divorced his wife, Latife Hanım, after less than two years of marriage.

1925-08-05.head: Welsh Nationalist Party Founded
1925-08-05.body: A Welsh nationalist party, Plaid Genedlaethol Cymru, has been founded at Pwllheli.

1925-08-06.head: Death of Sir Surendranath Banerjea
1925-08-06.body: Sir Surendranath Banerjea, 76, veteran of Indian nationalism and founder of the Indian National Association, has died at Barrackpore.

1925-08-06.head: Soviet General Kotovsky Assassinated
1925-08-06.body: General Grigory Kotovsky, the Red Army cavalry commander, has been shot dead near Odessa by a former associate.

1925-08-07.head: Druze Hold Jabal After French Defeat
1925-08-07.body: Following the defeat at al-Mazraa, French authority in the Jabal Druze has collapsed save for the besieged garrison at Suwayda.
1925-08-07.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-08-07.head: Oba of Lagos Deposed
1925-08-07.body: The colonial government of Nigeria has removed Eshugbayi Eleko from his position as Oba of Lagos.
1925-08-07.note: Date approximate; reported in the first week of August.

1925-08-08.head: Klan Parades in Washington
1925-08-08.body: Some 40,000 members of the Ku Klux Klan marched down Pennsylvania Avenue in Washington.

1925-08-09.head: Train Robbed at Kakori
1925-08-09.body: Indian revolutionaries have held up a train at Kakori, near Lucknow, and carried off Government treasure.

1925-08-10.head: Briand and Chamberlain Confer in London
1925-08-10.body: M. Aristide Briand, the French Foreign Minister, has arrived in London for conversations with Mr Austen Chamberlain on the proposed security pact.

1925-08-10.head: Belgian War Debt Talks Open
1925-08-10.body: Belgian and American delegates have opened talks in Washington for the funding of Belgium's war debt.

1925-08-11.head: Germany Raises Colonial Question
1925-08-11.body: Germany has indicated that the return of at least some of her former colonies would be a condition of her entry into the League of Nations.

1925-08-11.head: Druze and French Negotiate Prisoners
1925-08-11.body: Negotiations have opened between the French and Sultan al-Atrash for an exchange of prisoners taken at al-Mazraa.

1925-08-12.head: Azhar Ulama Condemn Sheikh Ali Abd al-Raziq
1925-08-12.body: The Council of Grand Ulama of al-Azhar has condemned Sheikh Ali Abd al-Raziq for his book 'Islam and the Principles of Government' and expelled him from the body of ulama.

1925-08-13.head: Raziq Verdict Stirs Cairo Controversy
1925-08-13.body: The al-Azhar verdict against Sheikh Ali Abd al-Raziq has aroused sharp controversy in Cairo, with the Liberal Constitutionalists defending him.
1925-08-13.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-08-14.head: Norway Takes Over Spitsbergen
1925-08-14.body: Norway has formally assumed sovereignty over Spitsbergen as the Svalbard Treaty came into force.

1925-08-14.head: Druze Exchange Prisoners with French
1925-08-14.body: The exchange of prisoners between the French and the Druze was concluded at Umm Walad.

1925-08-15.head: Seamen's Strike Spreads Overseas
1925-08-15.body: The British seamen's strike against the wage reduction has spread to ships in Dominion ports, holding up sailings.
1925-08-15.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-08-16.head: Zionist Delegates Gather in Vienna
1925-08-16.body: Delegates are gathering in Vienna for the Fourteenth Zionist Congress, amid police precautions against hostile demonstrations.
1925-08-16.note: Congress opened 18 August; preparations reported in the preceding days.

1925-08-17.head: French Reinforcements for Syria
1925-08-17.body: France has been sending reinforcements to Syria after the reverses in the Jabal Druze; General Michaud has been recalled.
1925-08-17.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-08-18.head: Zionist Congress Opens in Vienna
1925-08-18.body: The Fourteenth Zionist Congress has opened in Vienna under Dr Chaim Weizmann; police guarded the hall against anti-Semitic demonstrators.

1925-08-18.head: Belgian Debt Agreement Signed
1925-08-18.body: The United States and Belgium have signed an agreement for the settlement of Belgium's war debt.

1925-08-18.head: Steamer Boiler Explosion Kills Dozens
1925-08-18.body: A boiler explosion on the excursion steamer Mackinac off Newport, Rhode Island, killed more than forty passengers.

1925-08-19.head: Palestine Debated at Zionist Congress
1925-08-19.body: The Zionist Congress at Vienna has been debating immigration and colonisation in Palestine.
1925-08-19.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-08-20.head: Canton Minister Liao Zhongkai Assassinated
1925-08-20.body: Mr Liao Zhongkai, Finance Minister of the Nationalist Government at Canton, was shot dead outside Kuomintang headquarters.

1925-08-20.head: Canton Bars British and Japanese Ships
1925-08-20.body: The Canton authorities have forbidden British and Japanese ships to enter or leave Kwangtung ports.

1925-08-21.head: Arrests Follow Canton Murder
1925-08-21.body: The Canton government has made arrests following the assassination of Liao Zhongkai.
1925-08-21.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-08-22.head: Suwayda Still Holding Out
1925-08-22.body: The French garrison in the citadel of Suwayda continued to hold out against the Druze for a second month.
1925-08-22.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-08-23.head: Sultan al-Atrash Calls Syrians to Arms
1925-08-23.body: Sultan al-Atrash has issued a proclamation calling on all Syrians to rise against the French mandate.

1925-08-24.head: Mustafa Kemal Appears in Panama Hat
1925-08-24.body: President Mustafa Kemal arrived at Kastamonu wearing a European panama hat, in a tour of the Black Sea provinces.

1925-08-25.head: Allies Leave Düsseldorf and Duisburg
1925-08-25.body: French and Belgian troops have evacuated Düsseldorf, Duisburg and Ruhrort, ending the sanctions occupation begun in 1921.

1925-08-25.head: Lord Plumer for Palestine
1925-08-25.body: Field-Marshal Lord Plumer's appointment as High Commissioner for Palestine, in succession to Sir Herbert Samuel, was gazetted in Jerusalem.

1925-08-26.head: Seamen's Strike Holds Up Shipping
1925-08-26.body: The seamen's strike has continued to hold up British shipping in Australian and South African ports.
1925-08-26.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-08-27.head: Mustafa Kemal Defends the Hat
1925-08-27.body: Speaking at İnebolu, President Mustafa Kemal defended the wearing of the European hat by Turks as civilised dress, rejecting religious objections.

1925-08-28.head: Rif Fighting on the Ouergha
1925-08-28.body: French troops have continued fighting Abd el-Krim's Riffians along the Ouergha front in Morocco, as France and Spain prepare joint operations.
1925-08-28.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-08-29.head: Syrian Revolt Spreads Beyond Jabal
1925-08-29.body: Unrest has spread from the Jabal Druze to the Hauran and districts near Damascus following the proclamation of Sultan al-Atrash.
1925-08-29.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-08-30.head: Kemal's Hat Tour Continues
1925-08-30.body: President Mustafa Kemal continued his tour of Kastamonu province, urging Turks to adopt civilised dress.
1925-08-30.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-08-31.head: Zionist Congress Closes in Vienna
1925-08-31.body: The Fourteenth Zionist Congress has concluded its sessions in Vienna.

1925-09-01.head: Seaplanes Attempt Flight to Hawaii
1925-09-01.body: Commander John Rodgers of the United States Navy has taken off from California in the seaplane PN-9 No. 1 on an attempted flight to Hawaii.

1925-09-01.head: Chile Hands Tarata to Peru
1925-09-01.body: Chile has formally transferred the department of Tarata to Peru at a ceremony in the town.

1925-09-01.head: Danish Seamen Strike
1925-09-01.body: Danish seamen have struck over wages, adding to strikes disrupting shipping in the British Empire and China.

1925-09-02.head: Turkey Orders Officials into Hats
1925-09-02.body: The Turkish Council of Ministers has decreed that civil servants must wear hats, and forbidden robes and turbans to all but recognised clergy.

1925-09-02.head: Turkey Closes Dervish Lodges
1925-09-02.body: A decree has closed the religious lodges and dervish tekkes of Turkey.

1925-09-02.head: Albanian National Bank Opens
1925-09-02.body: The National Bank of Albania has been inaugurated at Durazzo.

1925-09-03.head: Airship Shenandoah Wrecked in Ohio
1925-09-03.body: The United States Navy airship Shenandoah broke up in a storm near Caldwell, Ohio, killing 14 of her 43 crew.

1925-09-03.head: Pétain Given Command in Morocco
1925-09-03.body: Marshal Pétain has been appointed commander-in-chief of the French forces in Morocco.

1925-09-03.head: Bolivian President Resigns
1925-09-03.body: President Bautista Saavedra of Bolivia has resigned; Señor Felipe Guzmán has succeeded him and fixed new elections for December.

1925-09-04.head: Rodgers Seaplane Missing in Pacific
1925-09-04.body: No word has been received from Commander Rodgers' seaplane PN-9 No. 1, missing on its flight to Hawaii; warships are searching.
1925-09-04.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-09-05.head: Colonel Mitchell Assails Air Administration
1925-09-05.body: Colonel William Mitchell has publicly accused the War and Navy Departments of incompetence and almost treasonable administration of national defence after the Shenandoah disaster.

1925-09-05.head: Canadian Parliament Dissolved
1925-09-05.body: Mr Mackenzie King has announced the dissolution of the Canadian Parliament, with a general election on 29 October.

1925-09-05.head: Riffians Advance on Tetuan
1925-09-05.body: Abd el-Krim's forces have launched an offensive toward Tetuan in Spanish Morocco.

1925-09-06.head: Syrian Rebels Executed at Aleppo
1925-09-06.body: The French have executed twelve Syrian rebels by firing squad at Aleppo, among them Mahmoud al-Ayyash.

1925-09-06.head: Liner Sophocles Returns to Cape Town
1925-09-06.body: The liner Sophocles was forced back to Cape Town when striking seamen barricaded themselves aboard and refused to work.

1925-09-07.head: League Assembly Opens at Geneva
1925-09-07.body: The sixth Assembly of the League of Nations has opened at Geneva.

1925-09-07.head: Death of René Viviani
1925-09-07.body: M. René Viviani, 62, Prime Minister of France at the outbreak of the war, has died.

1925-09-08.head: Spanish Troops Land at Alhucemas
1925-09-08.body: Spanish forces, supported by French warships, have landed at Alhucemas Bay in the heart of Abd el-Krim's Rif country.

1925-09-08.head: Shanghai Police Fire on Demonstrators
1925-09-08.body: Rioting occurred in Shanghai when British-officered police fired on some 2,000 demonstrators protesting the unequal treaties.

1925-09-09.head: Spaniards Consolidate Alhucemas Beachhead
1925-09-09.body: Spanish troops, landing tanks, have secured their beachhead at Alhucemas Bay.

1925-09-09.head: Amundsen to Fly Italian Airship
1925-09-09.body: Captain Amundsen has agreed to use the Italian airship N-1 for a fresh attempt on the North Pole next year.

1925-09-10.head: Missing Rodgers Crew Found Alive
1925-09-10.body: Commander Rodgers and his crew, missing nine days, were found near Kauai, having rigged a sail and sailed their seaplane some 450 miles.

1925-09-10.head: Pétain Opens Offensive in Morocco
1925-09-10.body: French troops under Marshal Pétain have opened an offensive against the Riffians north of the Ouergha.

1925-09-10.head: Riffians Encircle Tetuan
1925-09-10.body: Abd el-Krim's forces have surrounded Tetuan.

1925-09-11.head: Combined Rif Offensive Proceeds
1925-09-11.body: French and Spanish forces pressed their converging offensives against Abd el-Krim from the Ouergha and from Alhucemas Bay.
1925-09-11.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-09-12.head: Powers Agree on Security Pact
1925-09-12.body: The British, French and German governments have agreed in principle on a Western security pact and begun planning a conference.

1925-09-13.head: Security Conference Plans Advance
1925-09-13.body: Arrangements for a conference of Foreign Ministers on the Western security pact went forward following agreement in principle.
1925-09-13.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-09-14.head: League Assembly Debates Arbitration
1925-09-14.body: The League Assembly at Geneva has been debating arbitration, security and disarmament.
1925-09-14.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-09-15.head: French Occupy al-Musayfirah
1925-09-15.body: A French force of some 700 men from General Gamelin's command occupied al-Musayfirah in the Hauran and began fortifying it against the Druze.

1925-09-16.head: Druze Attack French at Musayfirah
1925-09-16.body: Druze rebels launched heavy night attacks against the French entrenched at al-Musayfirah.

1925-09-17.head: Druze Repulsed at Musayfirah
1925-09-17.body: The Druze assault on al-Musayfirah was beaten off with heavy loss by machine-gun fire and aircraft, the first French victory of the revolt.

1925-09-18.head: French Prepare Advance on Suwayda
1925-09-18.body: After the victory at al-Musayfirah, General Gamelin has been massing troops for the relief of the Suwayda garrison.
1925-09-18.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-09-19.head: Mosul Question Referred to Hague Court
1925-09-19.body: The League Council has asked the Permanent Court of International Justice for an advisory opinion on its powers in the Mosul frontier dispute between Turkey and Iraq.

1925-09-19.head: Gamelin Reaches Musayfirah
1925-09-19.body: General Gamelin has arrived at al-Musayfirah to take command of the column for the Jabal Druze.

1925-09-20.head: Turkish Protest Over Mosul Referral
1925-09-20.body: Turkey has objected to the League Council's handling of the Mosul question, maintaining that any settlement requires her consent.
1925-09-20.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-09-21.head: French Column Marches on Suwayda
1925-09-21.body: General Gamelin's column of some 8,000 men has marched from al-Musayfirah toward Suwayda, meeting little resistance.

1925-09-22.head: Gamelin Nears Suwayda
1925-09-22.body: The French relief column has advanced into the Jabal Druze toward the besieged citadel of Suwayda.
1925-09-22.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-09-23.head: Spaniards Push Inland from Alhucemas
1925-09-23.body: Spanish troops have extended their beachhead at Alhucemas Bay toward Ajdir, the seat of Abd el-Krim.
1925-09-23.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-09-24.head: Suwayda Relieved by French
1925-09-24.body: General Gamelin's column has entered Suwayda, relieving the French garrison besieged by the Druze since July.

1925-09-25.head: American Submarine S-51 Sunk
1925-09-25.body: The United States submarine S-51 was sunk in collision with the steamer City of Rome off Block Island; only three of her crew survived.

1925-09-26.head: League Assembly Concludes Session
1925-09-26.body: The sixth Assembly of the League of Nations has concluded its session at Geneva.
1925-09-26.note: Closing date given as reported; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly.

1925-09-26.head: Germany Accepts Security Conference
1925-09-26.body: Germany has accepted the invitation to a conference of Foreign Ministers on the security pact, to meet at Locarno in October.
1925-09-26.note: Date approximate; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly.

1925-09-27.head: Yellow River Floods in Shantung
1925-09-27.body: The Yellow River has overflowed its banks in Shantung province, China, drowning hundreds.
1925-09-27.note: Date approximate; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly.

1925-09-28.head: Druze Resist Despite Suwayda Relief
1925-09-28.body: Druze bands have continued to harass French columns in the Jabal Druze despite the relief of Suwayda.
1925-09-28.note: Ongoing story; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly, so this development is given as reported around this date.

1925-09-29.head: Death of Léon Bourgeois
1925-09-29.body: M. Léon Bourgeois, 74, former Prime Minister of France, a founder of the League of Nations and Nobel Peace laureate, has died.

1925-09-30.head: Pangalos Dissolves Greek Parliament
1925-09-30.body: General Theodoros Pangalos, head of the Greek Government, has dissolved the Parliament.
